full_judgment:
9. Mr. J. N. Deb, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant petitioner submits that the court of appeal below while decreeing the suit failed to consider that the suit was bad for defect of parties inasmuch as from Exhibit-2, Patta no. 74 there are as many as 26 Pattaders, all of them were not impleaded in the present suit for partition and as such committed an error of law which resulted in an error in the decision and occasioned failure of justice. He next submits that the Court of appeal below while decreeing the suit failed to appreciate that it appears from Patta No. 74, containing dag nos. 407 and 898 which subsequently recorded in Khatian No. 22 with dag Nos. 627, 604 and 628 having an area of .26, .17 and .38 acres respectively and all these lands except Dag No. 628 were not brought into the present suit and thereupon, the suit is bad for non-inclusion of all the ejmali property in the suit and as such committed an error of law which resulted in an error in the decision and occasioned failure of justice. 

 10. Mr. J. N. Deb, in the course of his argument upon placing the deposition of witnesses and exhibits submits that the court of appeal below while decreeing the suit failed to consider that neither there was any partition between the heirs of Safor Ali nor Safor Ali was the exclusive owner of the disputed Patta and Khatian and as such the transfer dated 04.11.1982 by some of the heirs of Safor Ali in favour of Abu Bakkar was illegal and mere paper transaction. He further submits that the Court of appeal below while decreeing the suit failed to appreciate that the defendant side by adducing evidence has been able to prove that the plaintiff is nothing but a permissive possessor and as such committed an error of law which resulted in an error in the decision and occasioned failure of justice. Mr. Deb, finally argues that the plaintiffs suit for partition is not maintainable inasmuch as admittedly daughters of deceased Safor Ali transmitted the suit property from an undivided plot without any amicable partition and admittedly no records of right was prepared in the name of the daughters of deceased Safor Ali rather, the records of right prepared in the name of the sons of deceased Safor Ali and as such the instant suit for simple partition without a prayer for declaration of title in the suit property is not maintainable. Mr. J. N. Deb in support of his submission relies on the decisions reported in 43 DLR(AD) 87, 49 DLR(AD) 68, 51 DLR(AD) 155, 10 PLR(Dhaka)27 and 6 BLD(AD) 109. 

 13. On perusal of the materials on record, it appears that admittedly the suit property originally belonged by one Safor Ali, who died leaving behind two sons and three daughters and later on, two daughters of Safor Ali and one Mirullah, husband of Sahar Banu transferred .081/4 acres of land to Haji Abu Bakkar by registered deed dated 4.11.1982 without any partition or amicable settlement between the heirs of deceased Safor Ali and thereafter, the said Haji Abu Bakkar ( PW-i) transferred the suit land to plaintiff -appellant-opposite party by executing a registered deed dated 01.4.1987. It further appears from Exhibit-2& Exhibit-Ka, Patta No-74, the name of Safor Ali struck off by replacing Pattader No-14, Sayed Ali and Pattader No-15, Budai as per order dated 16.07.1938 and corrected the same vide order dated 14.10.1938, which proved that Safor Ali was no longer remains pattader and the name of Syed Ali also subsequently has been struck off by replacing Pattader Nos. 17-21, vide order dated 12.06.1941 and corrected the same by order dated 16.12.1941. It also appears from Exhibit-7, D.P. Khatian No.zz and Exhibit - (Kha) Printed S.A. Khatian No. 27 that the same prepared in the name of Boudai Miah, son of Safor All along with others but neither in the Patta No. 74 nor in S.A. Khatian the name of the daughters of Safor All were recorded and the contents of the deed dated 4.11.1982 do not, disclose that the daughters of Safor Ali transferred their share out of .38 acres of land under Dag No.628 and Khatian No.22 inherited by z(two) sons and 3(three) daughters of Safor  Ali. Therefore, I am unable to agree with the finding of the Court of appeal below that the trial Court committed illegality in holding that the plaintiff failed to prove his vendor's or predecessor's exclusive possession and title in the suit land. 

 14. Upon an exhaustive consideration of the oral and documentary evidence on record, I find nothing on record to suggest that the daughters of Safor Ali had any exclusive right, title and possession in the suit land and the records of right also not prepared in their name though the Court of appeal below at its own motion arrived at a finding that after the death of Safor Ali his 2 sons and 3 daughters inherited .38 acres of land of Dag No.628 corresponding to Khatian No.22 and as such 3 (three) daughters were entitled to get share of 1410/21 acres out of which they sold only .081/4 acres to the vendor of the plaintiff-petitioner. I have already indicated that there being nothing on record to suggest that the daughters of Safor Ali were in exclusive possession at any time over the suit land and admittedly, the daughters of Safor Ali without any partition transferred their unspecified share on the basis of their own calculation though from Exhibit-2, Patta No.74 it appears that the name of Safor Ali has been struck off by replacing his sons being Pattader No-14 Sayed Ali and Pattader No.I5, Budai as per order of the revenue authority dated 16.07.1938 and neither in the Patta No. 74 nor in S.A. Khatian the name of the alleged daughters of Safor Ali were mentioned in any manner. Practically, from the evidence on record so far right, title and possession of the alleged the daughters of Safor Ali in the suit land is nil. SO, the reasons given by the learned judge of the lower appellate Court for passing the decree in favour of the plaintiff is not sustainable either in law or on facts.
